newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE sends mission to Albania, expresses concern.
newsitem.headline: OSCE sends mission to Albania, expresses concern.

text.p: Europe's top security body, the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), said on Tuesday it would send a fact-finding mission to Albania, where a state of emergency has been declared.

In a statement released at its Vienna headquarters, the OSCE said it had appointed former Austrian chancellor Franz Vranitzky to travel to Albania as soon as possible and assess the situation in the troubled Balkan nation.
An OSCE spokeswoman told Reuters she expected Vranitzky to travel to the Albanian capital Tirana within days and that he would stay for a few days.
"This mission has been agreed upon and Vranitzky has accepted," she said.
Albania's government declared emergency rule on Monday after a wave of violent unrest, sparked by the collapse of several fraudulent investment schemes, swept the country.

More than 20 people have been reported killed in Albania's south after enraged protesters stormed weapons depots and went on a rampage of burning and looting. A dusk-to-dawn curfew has been ordered and troops were called in to quell the unrest.

"The situation in Albania remains of great concern. There is an urgent need to stop the use of force, to re-establish stability and engage all political forces in dialogue on how to bring the country forward," the statement by the OSCE's chairman-in-office, Danish Foreign Minister Niels Herveg Petersen, said.
"Against this background, I have appointed former chancellor Franz Vraniztky as my personal representative to Albania," the statement continued.

Vranitzky's mission was to recommend action to the OSCE in order to "further the respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms", to uphold the rule of law and initiate dialogue between all political forces in Albania, it said.

The OSCE added it had instructed Vranitzky to assure the Albanian government of President Sali Berisha of its readiness to assist in resolving the crisis that has engulfed the country, "possibly in cooperation with other relevant international organisations".
